name: Vellum
description: A light, airy changelog of summaries: each day once in a wide date gutter beside a hairline rail, big tight titles, the people who shipped it, tag pills and a round feed button — and a release page with its facts in a side column.
features: Index layout: gutter (260px, hairline rail, no dots), one date per day
Summaries only, with a “Read release” link
Authors as avatars and names on every release
Tag pills, search and a round subscribe icon on the title row
Release page: side column with date, reading time and copy/share actions
Zero custom CSS — every detail is a theme setting

attrs.heading: Subscribe to the changelog
attrs.body: One email when something ships. No marketing.

posts.title: Observability for every deployment
posts.markdown:
Every deployment now records request logs, function durations and cache hits for seven days, with no setup and no extra cost on any plan.

## Added

![Request logs grouped by route](/api/assets/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000106)

- Logs filter by route, status code and region.
- A per-deployment summary shows the slowest routes first.

Placeholder release notes.

posts.title: Preview comments on mobile
posts.markdown:
Comments on preview deployments now work on phones and tablets, with the same threads and mentions as on a desktop.

## Changed

- The toolbar collapses into one button on narrow screens.
- Screenshots attached on mobile keep the device frame.

Placeholder release notes.

posts.title: Build cache keyed by lockfile
posts.markdown:
The build cache is now keyed by your lockfile, so a dependency change restores the right cache instead of starting cold.

## Fixed

- Monorepos with several lockfiles restore each package's own cache.

Placeholder release notes.

posts.title: Node.js 18 builds are deprecated
posts.markdown:
New builds on Node.js 18 will stop on the date below. Existing deployments keep serving traffic.

## Upgrading

Set the Node.js version to 20 or 22 in your project settings, or in `engines.node` in `package.json`, and redeploy. Builds still on 18 after the cut-off fail with a message that names this page.

Placeholder release notes.

posts.title: Edge config in the command line
posts.markdown:
Read and write edge config items from the command line, and pull them into local development with one command.

## Added

- `edge-config get`, `set` and `pull`.
- Values are typed when your project uses TypeScript.
